newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Hijacked Ethiopian plane crashed in sea - official.
newsitem.headline: Hijacked Ethiopian plane crashed in sea - official.

text.p: A hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 with about 178 passengers and crew aboard crashed into the sea near the Comoro Islands on Saturday, Guenet Berhe, a senior official with the airline, told Reuters.
She said she believed there were some survivors. The identity and motives of the hijackers were unknown, she added.
The plane was hijacked on Saturday morning shortly after takeoff from Addis Ababa on a scheduled flight -- number ET 961 -- to Abidjan via Nairobi, Brazzaville and Lagos.
After the hijackers took control, the plane entered Tanzanian airspace and then flew east across the Indian Ocean, heading for the Comoro Islands.
A telephone operator at Hotel Le Gallwa in Comoros, told Reuters in a telephone call:

"The wreck is about one km (half a mile) off the beach. Part of the fuselage is still afloat. Sixteen injured have been rescued and they are now searching for bodies." He said the plane had run out of fuel and rough seas were hampering rescue efforts.
